subject: Clarion Health — DPA scope, SCCs, and MSA/Order Form tie-outs
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <mruiz@clarionhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 08 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarion DPA questions and SCCs for MSA/order form — first review

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal and procurement have a handful of data-processing questions we need to close before the MSA/order form is finalized. High-level items:

- Which SCP/SCC module set do you rely on for EU-to-US transfers (controller->processor model)?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will act as a processor or a sub-processor for Clarion data in the dedicated deployment we discussed?
- We need a short transfer impact summary and any addenda you have for national transfer restrictions.
- Procurement also asked for an order-form template that calls out the data categories, retention, and subprocessor list.

I attached a short list of Clarion's initial questions (Clarion_DPA_v1_questions.pdf). Can you let us know which of these are already addressed in your standard DPA and what else you need from us (data locations, categories, third-party subprocessors)?

Our target is to sign the MSA + Order Form within the quarter, so a 48–72 hour turn on the DPA/SCC questions would be ideal. Thoughts on cadence?

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Clarion Health
mruiz@clarionhealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 08 May 2027 15:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarion DPA questions and SCCs for MSA/order form — first review

Hi Marta — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list.

Short answers up front:
- SCCs: Redwood uses the European Commission standard contractual clauses (module two/processor) as our baseline for hosted and dedicated customers; we also offer the new EU Commission Addendum where applicable.
- Role: For the deployment we discussed (dedicated capacity, customer-controlled VPC), Redwood is the processor; Clarion is the controller. We will provide the full subprocessors list and can commit to notice + approval flow for third-party infra services.
- Transfer impact: we do have a short Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) we provide for EU customers — I'll attach our redline and a brief executive summary.
- Order form: we have an MSA_OrderForm_Tieouts.xlsx with the standard fields; happy to pre-fill Clarion's values if you share data categories and estimated monthly tokens.

I'm attaching our initial redline (Redwood_DPA_v2_redline.pdf) and proposing a quick sync next week with Rishi (infrastructure/compliance) and Laura from legal to cover any carve-outs. Does Tue 11 May 10:00–11:00 ET work? If not, propose two windows and we'll accommodate.

Action items for Clarion: share the top 3 data categories you expect to send to the model and whether PHI or sensitive health identifiers will be included. Also confirm country of billing/contracting entity for SCC tailoring.

Thanks — we can move quickly on this.

— Soojin
Head of Field Compliance, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarion DPA questions and SCCs for MSA/order form — infrastructure notes

Marta / Soojin — quick technical notes for the record:

- Dedicated pools: Clarion's dedicated capacity will be isolated at the tenant layer; compute nodes are multi-tenant at the hypervisor level only if you opt for shared infra (you told us you prefer dedicated GPUs). We'll include the isolation statement in the DPA.
- Logging/retention: By default we keep request traces for 30 days; we can extend or reduce per the order form.
- Subprocessors: we use a small set of cloud infra and telemetry providers — we'll provide a current list and a commit to 30-day notice prior to changes.

I attached a short checklist for the transfer impact assessment we usually run — it lists the data flows and country hops we check. If Clarion can confirm whether EU-sourced data will be routed through US-based enrichment services, that would determine whether the TIA needs a narrower set of mitigations.

- Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarion DPA questions and SCCs for MSA/order form — draft redlines and SCC exhibit

Marta — attaching a tracked-change DPA and two supporting artifacts: an SCCs exhibit customized for Clarion and a draft Transfer Impact Addendum (Transfer-Impact-Addendum-draft.docx). Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-clarion-dpa-resources

Key callouts in the redline (summary):
- Roles: we kept "Processor" language but added explicit text around customer-controlled encryption keys for dedicated deployments (Section 2.3).
- Subprocessor approvals: proposed a notice + objection window (30 days) and a limited right to pause onboarding of a new subprocessor (escalation to legal).
- SCCs: used the EC processor-to-processor modules, with Clarion as controller; added localized attachments for restricted jurisdictions.
- Transfer Impact: draft includes a summary table of likely transfer paths and recommended mitigations (pseudonymization + contractual controls).

Open items for Clarion to confirm:
1) Data categories list (PHI vs non-PHI).
2) Whether Clarion requires HSM/KMS managed by Clarion (we can support either Redwood-managed KMS or customer-managed).
3) Any restrictions on telemetry/log retention beyond our standard 30 days.

I also pasted suggested language for a short Order Form section that pulls DPA references and retention periods into the commercial attachment.

If Clarion is comfortable, we can incorporate your edits and produce a final DPA + SCC exhibit for signature alongside the MSA. Otherwise, highlight the changes and we will schedule the legal sync.

Thanks — Laura
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 05:49:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Clarion DPA questions and SCCs for MSA/order form — Clarion responses

Laura / Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and the materials. A few answers from Clarion:

- Data categories: (1) patient identifiers (PHI), (2) operational metadata (non-PHI), (3) aggregated de-identified analytics. We expect some pipeline steps to include PHI before de-identification; our legal team will provide a short appendix this afternoon.
- KMS: Clarion prefers customer-managed KMS (we can provide key access via our cloud tenancy) for encryption of stored logs. Does Redwood have an installation process for customer KMS keys for the dedicated pool?
- Retention: procurement requests a 90-day retention for request traces (instead of 30). Clarion is willing to pay for extended retention if Redwood can provide a TCO estimate.

Procurement note: please include the Order Form fields for billing entity, billing address, estimated monthly tokens, and a SOC 2 attestation (current report or SOC2 Type II audit write-up). We're aiming to get commercial terms in parallel with legal.

Marta Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Clarion Health
